verdict.rationale: Self-hosting as a single dependency-free binary means you pay only for your own infrastructure, with no per-request fees. Community reports show large corpora running on modest fixed-cost servers ($8/mo for 1M records; 80M docs on a 64GB box). However, one team reports RAM usage scaling unpredictably with heavy search traffic, making it expensive. Another user cites a steep cloud jump from the free tier to $1200/month, a tier cliff, and indexing needs extra memory for bulk imports. Missing for 10: any first-party documentation of cloud pricing structure or usage-based limits/overage behavior, vendor guidance on resource sizing as data and query volume grow, and independent corroboration that costs stay predictable at scale.
